71e28936f0d54a5a451690483e86ac2562f671f7.summary: Press statement from the Illinois Attorney General's office, dated April 13, 2021. The office said its network had been compromised, discovered in the early hours of a Saturday. Staff and investigators were working with federal law enforcement to assess the extent of the compromise. The investigation was ongoing and further information was promised later. The report names no attacker, tools, techniques or CVEs.

dates.what: Attorney General's office announced its network had been compromised

subject.name: Illinois Attorney General's office network compromise

hedges: The investigation into the extent to which the Attorney General's office's network was compromised is ongoing.
Additional information will be made available at a later date.

71e6e667e19aa1e3fa3806e352442b214a4b67cc.summary: Blog entry on the SepSys ransomware, active from the second half of February 2020. It encrypts user files with AES and demands a $100 Bitcoin payment to a named recipient, Silicon Venom. Dropped files include README.html and destructy-1.0.exe, and the sample is said to masquerade as SMBGhoster_1.2.exe. Several security vendors detect it. The entry rates prevalence as low and lists the related Silvertor and RedRoman families.

7179be20ccd05bac5d29b6bdbcbe9c6c6db65aca.summary: Morphisec Labs reports a new, obfuscated variant of the JSSLoader .NET remote access trojan, delivered in 2022 through malicious Excel XLL add-in files. The report links JSSLoader to FIN7, which it calls a Russian criminal hacking group. The variant renames functions and splits strings to evade static scanners. The report says it adds no new capabilities, and it promotes Morphisec's own Moving Target Defense product.

71fe9012f8919629086bff9efea740d3d3e6b791.summary: WIRED article (28 May 2020) reporting an NSA advisory that Russia's GRU unit Sandworm has been exploiting a known vulnerability in the Exim mail transfer agent on email servers since at least August 2019. Per the advisory, Sandworm used compromised servers as an initial foothold: adding privileged users, disabling network security settings and changing secure shell configurations. Targets and motivation are not stated. Analysts from FireEye and Rendition Infosec discuss the risk, link Sandworm to earlier Ukraine, NotPetya and 2016 US election-board attacks, and recommend patching, log review…
